methodology: The decomposition process involved analyzing both the original research topic and the generated technical specification to extract independent and self-contained atomic units. Each atomic unit was evaluated for its technical specificity and clarity, ensuring that it could be implemented as a single requirement. The original research topic was broken down into its core functional requirements, while the generated specification was dissected to identify how well it addressed those requirements, including any additional details or clarifications provided.
mindtraced_atomic_units: DFFs must have an active high synchronous reset.
When reset is high, all outputs (q) should be set to zero.
DFFs should capture input data (d) on the positive edge of the clock (clk).
Output (q) reflects the captured data from input (d) when reset is low.
spec_atomic_units: Module defined as 'top_module' with inputs clk, d, reset and output q.
The module has 8 D flip-flops corresponding to the 8-bit input 'd'.
Reset signal sets all outputs (q) to zero when high.
DFFs capture input data (d) on the positive edge of clk.
Output (q) reflects the state of the D flip-flops based on input data and reset conditions.
Timing characteristics ensure reset must be stable before clk's positive edge.
Setup time for 'd' must be met before the rising edge of clk.
